You are being evaluated on Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream of ARC-style grid puzzles.
Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

In your continual harness, entries created without global_=True belong to this session and are lost with it.

### arc_task_729f2477_verified_upper_right_diagonal_rule 
 VERIFIED RULE: The square input has background 7 and four colored/noisy objects in its quadrants. Ignore and erase every object except the one in the UPPER-RIGHT quadrant; do not choose by color. That object is a noisy anti-diagonal. Replace the whole grid with 7, then draw a clean length-(n//2+1) anti-diagonal in the retained object color from input/output coordinate (0,n-1) through (n//2,n//2-1), i.e. cells (r,n-1-r) for r=0..n//2. Everything else is 7. Demo 1 (7x7) retained upper-right color 2 and output 2 at (0,6),(1,5),(2,4),(3,3), not color 0. Initial incorrect attempt mistakenly used the upper-left color 0, so quadrant selection is essential.

 ARC task-729f2477 TEST-VERIFIED RULE: Background is 7 and output keeps original dimensions. For each non-7 color, compute its full axis-aligned bounding-box area. Select the color with the largest area; pixel count is irrelevant. Erase every non-7 cell, then draw a full diagonal of the selected color in that color's original bounding-box region. Use main diagonal (top-left to bottom-right) when it best matches the selected object's existing cells; use anti-diagonal (top-right to bottom-left) when that matches better. If the bbox is rectangular, diagonal length is max(height,width), effectively extending the shorter dimension. Exactly one region encodes the task's diagonal: erase every non-7 cell, then draw the completed unit-slope main or anti-diagonal in that region's color and bounds. Selection pitfall: do NOT choose whichever region has the longest or densest apparent diagonal. Look for a seed on the region's outer/corner diagonal, which may be isolated, separated from its noisy cluster, and contain gaps, then complete the canonical corner-to-corner diagonal of the whole region.
